newsitem.title: USA: Investors choosier on new U.S corporate bond deals.
newsitem.headline: Investors choosier on new U.S corporate bond deals.

text.p: Despite generally good conditions in the U.S. corporate debt primary market, investor demand for new corporate issues has weakened slightly from ebullient levels of several weeks ago, syndicate officials said.
"Demand is still there, but investors are being choosy," said one high-grade syndicate official. "It isn't like two weeks ago where you could sell even the worst credit and it was oversubscribed."
One official said he was seeing more swaps in the new-issue market, suggesting investors were reluctant to commit new cash to the deals.
Investors will often spruce up their portfolios by exchanging bonds in their existing investory for new issues.
Market sources attributed the change in investor sentiment to an increase in overall uncertainty in the fixed-income markets.
They noted recent price weakness in the emerging and high-yield market began to hurt the investment grade bond market last week.
Comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan about inadequate pricing of risk among corporate bond spreads are another factor, they said.
One recent example may be a $300 million offering of 30-year non-callable debt by Archer Daniels Midland Co which is expected to price later this afternoon.
Market sources said original price talk of a low-50 basis point spread was not being greeted kindly by investors.

Investors are demanding a price in the mid-50s, sources said. One market player said ADM's recent price-fixing scandal in which the company paid an unprecedented $100 million penalty may be affecting buyside attitudes.
Officials at Salomon Brothers Inc, the underwriter, declined to comment.

In the high-yield market, market sources said WinStar Communications Inc has restructured a high-yield offering expected to price on Wednesday afternoon as a result of slack investor demand for non-cash paying bonds from telecommunications companies.

WinStar, a wireless competitive local exchange carrier, has increased the price talk on an offering of $100 million in eight-year senior deferred interest notes to 14.5 percent from 13 3/4 percent to 14 percent.
Calls to Credit Suisse First Boston, the underwriter, were not immediately returned.
Returning to the high-grade market, other new issues expected for Wednesday include:
-a $200 million 12-year note offering from 360 Communications Corp via Salomon Brothers. Price talk is around 105 basis points over Treasuries, market sources said.
-a $400 million offering by Honeywell Inc of five- and 10-year notes via Bear Stearns Inc and JP Morgan Securities.
In the junk market, Hollinger International Inc, an international publishing company, is expected to sell $530 million in eight- and 10-year notes via Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.
The bonds are being sold by the company's finance unit, Hollinger International Publishing Inc.
((-Douglas Brown, 212-859-1662))
